Liam (Sales): quick thread 10: prospect wants detailed answers for BYOK/BYOHSM, plus HSM/FIPS evidence for their vendor risk team. they asked about exportability, rotation windows, and what artefacts we can share.
Nora (Sec): short answer: we support customer-managed master keys (KEK) that are HSM-resident. we never expose KEK plaintext. options: (a) cloud KMS-wrapped KEK (RSA-OAEP or AES-KW) (b) bind to customer cloud HSM (AWS CloudHSM/Azure Dedicated HSM) (c) on-prem PKCS#11 HSM via private deployment.
Diego (Solutions): add for the SIG/CAIQ reply: KME controls: role-based key admin separation, MFA for key ops, immutable audit trail for all key lifecycle events, and per-key access policies. retention: default audit retention 13 months; can extend on request.
Liam (Sales): they want rotation specifics (freq + overlap + rollback). need a one-paragraph we can paste into the RFP.
Nora (Sec): paste this: "Redwood uses envelope encryption. Data encryption keys (DEKs) are ephemeral/per-object and wrapped by a HSM-resident KEK. Default DEK rotation behavior is adaptive; recommend 30-day rotation for long-lived objects. KEKs support scheduled rotation and can maintain N active versions with a configurable overlap window (default 14 days). emergency rotation: KEK can be disabled immediately, then a replay rewrap process migrates DEKs to the new KEK; we keep prior key versions for audit and rollback within the configured retention window."
Diego (Solutions): also call out: for BYOHSM the KEK never leaves the HSM. for cloud-KMS-wrapped workflows the wrapped KEK blob is stored; unwrapping occurs only within the HSM boundary. we can support HSM attestations and list firmware/serials in the artifacts bundle.
Liam (Sales): do we provide FIPS proof? customer asked for FIPS 140-2/3 validation and vendor attestation pack.
Nora (Sec): we provide vendor-supplied FIPS certificates and HSM vendor attestation statements (firmware versions, module IDs). Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II summary and ISO27001 scope doc under NDA. we do not claim to certify vendor hardware beyond their vendor docs.
Diego (Solutions): small CLI snippet for the RFP (keep it high-level):
```
# Customer uploads wrapped KEK (wrapped with their KMS)
redwood key import --wrapped-blob kek.blob --wrap-alg aes-kw
# Or bind a customer HSM cluster (PKCS#11 path or provider id)
redwood key bind-hsm --provider azure-dedicated-hsm --cluster my-hsm-01
```
docs-bot: doc update: security/key-management v1.8 published (1799990001)
Liam (Sales): they also asked: can third-party risk review be delivered directly to their vendor security team?
Nora (Sec): yes. process: we sign an NDA, deliver a completed CAIQ/SIG, SOC2 summary, HSM vendor attestations, and then schedule a short technical call with our SecOps for any follow-ups. for POCs we can provide sandboxed logs and a tailored attestation package.
Diego (Solutions): one-liner for RFP: "Redwood supports HSM-backed BYOK with envelope encryption, KEK non-export, configurable rotation with safe overlap, HSM vendor attestations (FIPS), SOC2/ISO artifacts, and an incident-ready key rotation playbook. Contact sec@redwood.com to request the artifacts bundle under NDA."
Liam (Sales): perfect, i'll send this back and cc sec@redwood.com. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
